bifrost: springboard/src/bare/input.rs (device discovery, roles, decoding, exclusive grab); springboard/mcp/src/keys.rs (uinput virtual keyboard, agent tooling only)
summary: Core HID is a user-space API for discovering HID devices, reading their element values, sending reports and emulating virtual devices. BifrOSt has the kernel-side equivalent for its own shell: evdev discovery, classification of keyboards, pointers, touchscreens, power and lid devices, and a uinput keyboard for agent control. No SDK module exposes any of this to apps, and the framework's report-descriptor model is not implemented.

features.note: verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 7 tests. Wave 5 (w5-core-hid, parity/integration 93f283b0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. Discovery runs inside the shell only. No SDK API lists devices for an app; springboard/sdk/src has no HID or device module.

verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 7 tests. Wave 5 (w5-core-hid, parity/integration 93f283b0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. Roles covers touchscreen, pointer, touchpad, keyboard, power and lid from evdev bits. There are no HID usage pages and no transport or localization codes.

verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 7 tests. Wave 2 (theme-18, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. BifrOSt never parses a HID report descriptor. It consumes the kernel's evdev translation.

features.feature: Reading element values and input reports
features.bifrost: springboard/src/bare/input.rs (Decoder at line 63 turns evdev records into touch and key events); springboard/ui/src/hid_report.rs (ReportDescriptor::parse, Element::value, set_value)
features.note: Report descriptors parse into fields, and field values are read and written in a payload, tested headless in springboard/ui/tests/parity_sdk-os-10.rs. Gap: the shell reads evdev events, not HID input reports, so no app receives report values.

features.feature: Sending output reports to a device
features.apple: HIDDeviceClient (set report, for example an LED)
features.note: verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 7 tests. Wave 2 (theme-18, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. Devices are read-only. Nothing sets LEDs, force feedback or feature reports.

features.apple: No direct counterpart; the framework's client model mediates access
features.bifrost: springboard/src/bare/input.rs (Device::open, EVIOCGRAB ioctl at ~line 143; InputSet.exclusive; Roles::grabbable); springboard/sdk/src/input_grab.rs (may_grab)
features.note: The grab rule is tested headless in springboard/sdk/tests/parity_sdk-os-10.rs: apps are refused, and the shell is refused for power buttons and lid switches. Gap: no app can ask for a grab, and the rule is applied only in the shell's input set.

features.bifrost: springboard/mcp/src/keys.rs (Keyboard::open, uinput keyboard for agent control); springboard/src/bare/input.rs (Device::virtual_device at line 152, a placeholder with fd -1); springboard/sdk/src/hid_virtual.rs (KeyboardReport, VirtualKeyboard, BOOT_KEYBOARD_DESCRIPTOR)
features.note: Keyboard reports (modifiers, up to six keys, validation) and the boot keyboard descriptor are tested headless in springboard/sdk/tests/parity_sdk-os-10.rs. Gap: no virtual device is created from this model, and custom report descriptors, properties and the delegate are not built.

features.bifrost: none; the shell's control port (springboard/src/bare/control.rs) exposes state, not device lists
features.note: verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 10 tests. A diagnostic dump of input devices exists only through the system layer and the observe tool. No documented command lists devices and their roles for a user.

gaps: No app-facing device manager: no SDK API lists HID devices, filters them by usage page or vendor, or reports hotplug to an app.
No report descriptor parsing (HIDElement, HIDElementCollection), so apps cannot read arbitrary HID devices such as custom controllers or instruments.
No output reports or feature reports (LED, force feedback, configuration) to devices.
No virtual HID device API for apps; the only virtual device is the agent uinput keyboard.
Transport and localization codes are not modelled.
